jobs.title: Director Information Technology Operations
jobs.description:
The Director, IT Operations is responsible for the end-to-end management and performance of the organization's global IT operations function, including service management, enterprise applications, identity and access management, application support, and outsourced infrastructure services. The role ensures high-quality, secure, and cost-effective IT service delivery across multiple regions while driving operational excellence, vendor accountability, and technology optimization. A key focus is managing strategic vendor relationships, controlling infrastructure costs, improving service performance, and leveraging automation and AI solutions to enhance operational efficiency and business outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and oversee global IT operations, including IT service management, service desk, end-user support, enterprise applications, identity and access management, and production application support.
Own the operational management of outsourced infrastructure services, including vendor governance, service-level performance, escalations, and contract compliance.
Review, reconcile, and approve infrastructure invoices, ensuring alignment with contracted services and resolving billing discrepancies with vendors and internal stakeholders.
Maintain infrastructure asset inventories and service baselines to support cost control, operational transparency, and vendor management.
Develop, manage, and optimize IT service management processes, including request management, approvals, service catalogues, SLAs, and workflow automation.
Lead software licensing governance, audits, renewals, and optimization initiatives to improve compliance and reduce costs.
Drive the adoption of AI and automation tools to improve IT operations, reporting, service management, ticket triage, and process efficiency.
Serve as the senior escalation point for major incidents, coordinating cross-functional and vendor response efforts and providing executive-level communications.
Oversee identity and access management processes, including joiner, mover, and leaver activities, access controls, and privileged access governance.
Produce operational performance reports, monitor service metrics, manage risks, and support strategic decision-making.
Identify and implement cost reduction opportunities through vendor consolidation, contract optimization, licence rationalization, and sourcing strategies.
Lead, develop, and mentor IT operations teams, fostering accountability, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

8+ years of experience in IT operations, infrastructure management, or a related technology leadership role.
Demonstrated experience leading multi-region IT operations teams or managing large-scale outsourced infrastructure services.
Strong vendor and contract management expertise, including service-level agreements, cost controls, billing reconciliation, and contract governance.
Hands-on experience with IT service management platforms such as Jira Service Management or ServiceNow.
Advanced knowledge of Microsoft 365, Entra ID (Azure AD), Active Directory, Intune, and enterprise IT environments.
Experience in automation and scripting using tools such as PowerShell, Graph API, Jira Automation, or equivalent technologies.
Proven ability to leverage AI technologies, such as Copilot and other AI tools, to optimize operational processes and drive efficiency.
Strong incident, problem, and change management expertise in complex production environments.
Excellent analytical, financial, and commercial acumen, including budgeting, cost management, invoice validation, and vendor negotiations.
Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills.
Experience managing identity and access management processes and information security controls.
Proven people leadership, coaching, and team development capabilities.
Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and continuous improvement mindset.

Benefits

At Dye & Durham we strive to be visionaries! As a leader in our field, we ensure our employees are ready for the next challenge in their journey with us by offering internal and external training opportunities. We offer competitive salaries and a whole host of benefits including healthcare, pension, company discounts, wellness programs, and paid days off to move house or volunteer for your favourite charity.

In line with the amended Employment Standards Act 2000, the salary range for this role is:
$145K - $175K, dependent on assessment of skills during the interview process.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Architecture & Engineering
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director, Enterprise Architecture & Engineering based in Canada.

The Director, Enterprise Architecture & Engineering will set enterprise technical direction while building an engineering organization capable of scaling with a growing business. The role goes beyond Salesforce, connecting CRM, custom software, data, integration, cloud, security, DevOps, analytics, and AI into secure and resilient solutions. You will lead complex architecture decisions, establish engineering standards, and develop scalable approaches to AI and agentic systems. You will also manage engineers and technical leaders, strengthen technical leadership, and shape organizational capabilities. Working closely with executive client stakeholders, Sales, and Delivery, you will connect technology decisions to business outcomes and client value. This is a highly strategic and hands-on leadership opportunity for an experienced technology leader comfortable navigating complex environments, ambiguity, and rapid growth.

Accountabilities

Set enterprise architecture strategy, principles, decision rights, and reusable reference patterns across client engagements.
Lead complex architecture decisions and design reviews, balancing business value, security, scalability, reliability, maintainability, and cost.
Define how Salesforce, Apex, Python, APIs, data, integration, cloud services, and analytics work together across enterprise solutions.
Establish standardized engineering practices covering source control, peer review, automated testing, CI/CD, environments, release management, observability, rollback, and incident learning.
Develop production AI and agentic engineering standards covering data grounding, model and tool integration, evaluation, guardrails, human oversight, telemetry, security, cost, and lifecycle management.
Evaluate Salesforce Data 360/Data Cloud, Informatica, MuleSoft, Agentforce, Claude, cloud data platforms, and other technologies based on business requirements and architectural evidence.
Embed security, privacy, compliance, identity, access controls, encryption, secrets management, audit logging, resilience, vulnerability management, and incident response into engineering practices.
Manage engineers and technical leaders, overseeing hiring, performance, coaching, career development, succession planning, staffing, capacity, and team health.
Develop Principal- and Lead-level technical talent through clear expectations, capability paths, communities of practice, architecture reviews, and reusable examples.
Build trusted relationships with client CIOs, CTOs, enterprise architects, security leaders, data leaders, and platform owners.
Partner with Sales and Delivery on qualification, discovery, solution design, estimation, technical risk, executive presentations, and delivery commitments.
Connect technical strategy to client outcomes, delivery quality, operating costs, resilience, revenue, margins, pipeline, retention, and account growth.
Develop differentiated technical offerings, reference architectures, accelerators, and points of view that strengthen enterprise capabilities.
Establish lightweight governance and decision-making processes that improve technical quality without slowing delivery.

Requirements

10+ years of experience in enterprise architecture, solution architecture, engineering, or technical consulting, including leadership across complex client programs or technical capabilities.
Deep Salesforce architecture and engineering expertise, including Apex, Lightning, platform limits, data and sharing design, integration, security, environments, packaging, and release management.
Salesforce Certified Technical Architect certification is highly preferred.
Strong engineering expertise beyond Salesforce, including Python, APIs, event-driven architectures, SQL, JavaScript or TypeScript, testing, automation, and application design patterns.
Broad enterprise technology experience across Salesforce Data 360/Data Cloud, Informatica, MuleSoft or comparable integration platforms, cloud data platforms, AWS/Azure/GCP services, DevOps, and observability.
Proven production experience with AI or agentic systems, including grounding, orchestration, evaluation, guardrails, observability, security, cost management, human oversight, and lifecycle management.
Experience designing secure systems in regulated environments and translating requirements such as HIPAA, HITRUST, FedRAMP, NIST, SOC 2, and privacy obligations into practical technical controls.
Demonstrated ability to standardize CI/CD, automated quality and security controls, environment and release strategies, deployment evidence, rollback processes, and operational feedback across teams.
Significant people-management experience leading engineers and technical leaders, developing successors, and improving quality while fostering trust and accountability.
Proven experience scaling engineering organizations and contributing to business growth through talent development, operating systems, reusable technology, disciplined investment, and delivery excellence.
Strong executive, client, and commercial judgment, with the ability to communicate complex technical tradeoffs, make decisions through ambiguity, and remain accountable for outcomes.
Ability to work collaboratively across technical, commercial, and client-facing functions while maintaining momentum in complex and rapidly changing environments.

Benefits

$175,000–$275,000 compensation range.
Fully remote work within the United States or Canada.
Unlimited PTO.
Learning and development stipend for certifications, training, and conferences.
Wellness support through stipends and related initiatives.
Collaborative, values-driven culture.
Opportunities for professional advancement into senior leadership roles.
Opportunity to shape enterprise architecture, engineering, AI, and technical strategy at scale.

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance
jobs.description:
The Vice President, Finance, Americas
is responsible for providing strategic financial leadership and oversight across the Americas region. This role partners with executive and business leaders to drive financial performance, support growth initiatives, ensure compliance with financial and regulatory requirements, and deliver accurate financial planning, reporting, and analysis. The VP Finance leads regional finance functions, including accounting, budgeting, forecasting, tax, treasury, internal controls, and financial operations, while fostering a high-performing team and supporting the achievement of organizational objectives.

Reports to the Chief Financial Officer.

Responsibilities

1. Financial Reporting & Accounting

Oversee accounting operations for the Americas region, including general ledger, month-end/quarter-end closing, and consolidation.
Own inventory accounting for the Memphis distribution center — valuation methodology, standard costing, cycle counts, and obsolescence/reserve policy.
Ensure COGS accuracy and margin analysis tied to distribution operations.
Ensure accuracy of financial statements prepared in accordance with local GAAP in each jurisdiction (US, Canada, and LatAm countries).
Prepare and submit financial reports in compliance with IFRS and Group accounting standards, ensuring quality and compliance.
Coordinate with external auditors for annual audits, implement improvement plans, and maintain effective communication with internal and external audit teams.
Work closely with the HQ finance team to ensure consistency in reporting formats, policies, and processes.

2. Compliance

Maintain and enhance internal control and accounting procedures to align with Group policies and US/Canadian/LatAm regulations.
Ensure customs and bonded warehouse compliance — duty deferral, in-bond transfers, and CBP requirements — for the Memphis distribution center, partnering with trade compliance and logistics teams.
Ensure compliance with local direct and indirect tax regulations, including corporate income tax, VAT/GST, and multi-state US sales/use tax nexus; complete filings accurately and on time.
Regularly review the reasonableness of intercompany transfer pricing across US, Canada, and LatAm entities, and assess associated risks.

3. Treasury & Financial Planning

Manage cash-flow, working capital, and banking relationships across the Americas to ensure liquidity and efficient funding.
Support financing activities and treasury optimization.
Provide budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis to support operational decision-making across HQ, sales & marketing offices, and the distribution center.

4. System & Process Enhancement

Drive ERP system integration and automation to improve reporting efficiency, data accuracy, and close timelines.
Identify process improvement opportunities across order-to-cash and purchase-to-pay to enhance timeliness and reliability of financial information.

Qualifications and Experience

Bachelor's degree or above in Accounting, Finance, or related field; CPA/ACA/ACCA qualification preferred.
Minimum 15 years of accounting or finance experience, including at least 6 years in a managerial or Controller role.
Solid knowledge of IFRS, US/Canadian tax regulations, compliance, and internal controls.
Experience with distribution or logistics operations, including inventory accounting and customs/bonded warehouse environments, strongly preferred.
Hands-on SAP experience, particularly ERP implementation or migration, is a strong plus.
Previous experience in multinational or listed companies is a strong plus.
Proven leadership experience building and managing multi-country/multi-entity finance teams.
Strong written and verbal English communication skills for global stakeholder management. Chinese is a plus for Group-level communication.

Competencies (Skills & Behaviors)

Strong AI awareness with hands-on experience implementing AI tools or automation workflows within a finance environment.
Experience supporting regional or global finance functions.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Familiar with transfer pricing and cross-border tax principles.
Comfortable operating at senior leadership/executive committee level, with strong stakeholder management and influencing skills.
Familiar with inventory and sales/purchase management.

Leadership & Strategic Influence

Partner with Americas business, sales, and marketing leadership to provide financial insights, operational performance analysis, and cost control recommendations.
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing finance team across Montreal HQ, sales & marketing offices, and the Memphis distribution center; drive talent development and succession planning.
Act as a strategic finance partner to the Americas leadership team, contributing to regional business strategy, investment decisions, and capital allocation.
Report to the Group CFO on financial performance, risks, and strategic priorities, representing Americas Finance in Group-level executive discussions.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Regulatory Affairs (Regulatory Intelligence)
jobs.description:
Telix Pharmaceuticals is a dynamic, fast-growing radiopharmaceutical company with offices in Australia (HQ), Belgium, Japan, Switzerland, and the United States. Our mission is to deliver on the promise of precision medicine through targeted radiation. At our core, we exist to create products that seek to improve the quality of life for people living with cancer and rare diseases.
You will be supporting the international roll-out of our approved prostate cancer imaging agent and helping us to advance our portfolio of late clinical-stage products that address significant unmet need in oncology and rare diseases.

See Yourself at Telix

The Associate Director, Regulatory Affairs (Regulatory Intelligence), will be responsible for monitoring, analyzing, and interpreting global regulatory developments to ensure the company’s compliance and strategic positioning in the pharmaceutical market. This role involves collecting and disseminating regulatory information, providing insights to internal stakeholders, and supporting the development of regulatory strategies. Supports the Senior Director, Regulatory Affairs (Labeling/Ad-Promo), in efforts to influence the regulatory environment.

Key Accountabilities

Proactively monitors and assesses global regulatory environments for emerging changes in laws, regulations, and guidance impacting drug and device development.
Tracks and evaluates updates from key regulatory authorities (e.g., FDA, EMA), industry associations, and external intelligence sources.
Maintains and continuously enhances regulatory intelligence databases and tools to ensure accurate, timely, and efficient dissemination of information.
Analyzes regulatory developments, including guidance documents, policies, and regulations, to determine potential impact on internal processes, development programs, and regulatory strategies. Anticipates and tracks regulatory changes over time, delivering timely, accurate, and actionable updates to impacted stakeholders across the organization.
Partners with Quality to ensure appropriate change control processes are initiated and tracked through implementation when regulatory changes impact internal procedures.
Translates complex regulatory information into clear, actionable insights for cross-functional stakeholders.
Develops and delivers regulatory intelligence communications, including newsletters, alerts, trackers, and periodic reports.
Responds to internal inquiries by providing tailored regulatory intelligence summaries and detailed analyses to support decision-making.
Leads and facilitates regulatory intelligence meetings to include review and discussion of ad hoc query requests, regulatory background package requests, health authority guidance, Federal Register notices, public commenting opportunities, newsletter content, training sessions, and knowledge-sharing forums.
Coordinates cross-functional discussions to evaluate the impact of new or revised regulatory requirements. Collaborates closely with key functions, including Quality, Pharmacovigilance, Clinical, CMC, and Regulatory Affairs, to ensure alignment and effective implementation.
Leads the regulatory public commenting process and identifies opportunities to engage with external stakeholders on draft regulations, guidance, and policies.
Supports the development, coordination, and submission of company comments to regulatory authorities and industry organizations.
Confirms the list of upcoming regulatory meetings/workshops/conferences remains current.
Drives continuous improvement of regulatory intelligence processes, systems, and tools to enhance efficiency and value. Authors and conducts periodic review of regulatory intelligence Standard Operating Procedures or work practices.
Manages and maintains internal knowledge management platforms (e.g., SharePoint, intranet) to ensure accessible and up-to-date information. Develops, reviews and updates the Regulatory Intelligence homepage on the Global Regulatory Affairs Portal.
Contributes to cross-functional initiatives and organizational projects by providing regulatory intelligence expertise and strategic insight.
Manages onboarding and offboarding of regulatory intelligence team members and provides input on team member performance. Provides leadership, coaching, and day‑to‑day oversight for direct reports within Global Regulatory Intelligence, fostering their professional growth and development.

Position Requirements

Education and Experience:

Bachelor's degree in life sciences, law, public policy, or a related field.
A Master's degree or higher is preferred.
Minimum 8 years’ experience in pharmaceutical regulatory affairs, including 6 years’ experience in regulatory intelligence.
Demonstrates solid working knowledge of the drug, biologic, and device development process, laws, regulations, and guidelines from FDA, EMA, PMDA, ICH, etc.
Demonstrates understanding of the major regional and global industry association priorities (e.g., PhRMA, EFPIA, JPMA, etc.).
Previous interactions with FDA or other health authority are desirable.
Proficient in using regulatory intelligence tools and databases.

Key Competencies

Analytical thinking, problem solving and decision making: Demonstrates strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to evaluate complex issues, identify risks and opportunities, develop practical and achievable solutions, and make sound, data-driven decisions
Strategic thinking & regulatory innovation: Capable of strategic thinking and proposing innovative solutions involving regulatory issues, while being a team player who invites response and discussion
Performance & accountability: Comfortable in a fast-paced, results-driven, and highly accountable work environment
Independence & team effectiveness: Demonstrated ability to work independently with minimal supervision while also contributing effectively as a collaborative team member. Balances individual accountability with a commitment to supporting team goals, sharing knowledge, and fostering a positive and productive work environment.
Attention to detail: Strong attention to detail, ensuring accuracy, quality, and consistency in all work products
Multitasking: Demonstrates the ability to effectively prioritize, organize, and manage multiple tasks, projects, and competing priorities simultaneously while meeting deadlines and maintaining high standards of performance

Key Capabilities

Commitment to excellence: Take pride in your work and consistently strive for excellence in everything you do
Results-oriented: Driven to achieve goals and objectives, with a strong focus on delivering measurable results
Creativity and innovation: Possess a willingness to think outside the box and come up with unique and creative solutions to challenges
Strong communication skills: Able to communicate effectively with colleagues and stakeholders at all levels, using clear and concise language
Collaboration: Work effectively as part of a team, actively sharing knowledge and expertise to achieve common goals
Resilience: Demonstrate the ability to bounce back from setbacks and persevere in the face of challenges
Inclusive mindset: Demonstrate an understanding and appreciation for diversity, and actively work to create an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and respected
Adaptability: Comfortable working in a dynamic environment, able to adjust to changing priorities, and willing to take on new challenges
Ethical behavior: Act with integrity and demonstrate a commitment to ethical behavior in all interactions with colleagues and stakeholders
Continuous learning: Show a commitment to ongoing learning and professional development, continually seeking out opportunities to expand your knowledge and skills

At Telix, we believe everyone counts
, we strive to be extraordinary
, and we pursue our goals with determination and integrity
. You will be part of an engaged and supportive group of colleagues who all have a shared purpose: to help people with cancer and rare diseases live longer, better quality lives.
Being a Telix employee means being a part of a unique, global, interdisciplinary team working to deliver what's next in precision medicine. We have hybrid and remote employees located all around the world. We offer competitive salaries, annual performance-based bonuses, an equity-based incentive program, generous vacation, paid wellness days and support for learning and development.

Telix Pharmaceuticals is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other legally protected characteristics.

jobs.title: Director Information Security
jobs.description:
The Director, Information Security (InfoSec) is responsible for leading and evolving the organisation's global information security function, ensuring the protection of corporate systems, employee productivity platforms, customer-facing products, data, and technology assets. This role will define and execute the security strategy, strengthen cyber resilience, manage security risk, and implement scalable security controls that support business growth and regulatory compliance.

The successful candidate will build and mature security capabilities from the ground up, improving legacy environments, embedding security best practices across the organisation, and ensuring robust monitoring, governance, and risk management frameworks are in place. Through strong leadership and technical expertise, this role will have a significant impact on safeguarding the organisation, supporting customer trust, and enabling secure business operations globally.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the global information security function and provide strategic direction across all security domains.
Develop and implement the organisation's information security strategy, operating model, and roadmap.
Oversee security for corporate platforms, including email, collaboration, and productivity tools.
Ensure the security of customer-facing products, applications, and technology services.
Build and mature security capabilities and processes, establishing scalable security programmes from the ground up.
Identify, assess, and mitigate cyber security risks through effective governance and risk management practices.
Lead vulnerability management, penetration testing, threat detection, and ongoing security monitoring activities.
Implement compensating controls to address audit findings, compliance requirements, and identified risks.
Improve and modernise legacy systems while maintaining appropriate security controls and business continuity.
Partner with technology, infrastructure, engineering, product, legal, privacy, and risk teams to embed security-by-design principles.
Lead incident response planning, preparedness, and crisis management activities.
Develop executive reporting, security metrics, and dashboards to communicate security posture and programme maturity.
Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing Information Security team.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

10+ years of experience in Information Security, Cyber Security, Technology Risk, or related technology leadership roles.
Experience building, transforming, or scaling security functions within growing organisations.
Strong technical foundation in infrastructure, IT operations, systems administration, networking, or network security.
Demonstrated experience leading security operations, vulnerability management, penetration testing, and incident response programmes.
Strong understanding of security frameworks and industry standards such as ISO 27001, NIST, CIS Controls, SOC 2, and PCI DSS.
Experience implementing governance, risk, and compliance frameworks, including audit remediation and compensating controls.
Knowledge of cloud security, identity and access management, application security, and secure software development practices.
Proven ability to communicate technical risks and security priorities to executive and non-technical stakeholders.
Strong leadership, stakeholder management, and team development capabilities.
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, CCSP, or equivalent are highly desirable.

Benefits

At Dye & Durham we strive to be visionaries! As a leader in our field, we ensure our employees are ready for the next challenge in their journey with us by offering internal and external training opportunities. We offer competitive salaries and a whole host of benefits including healthcare, pension, company discounts, wellness programs, and paid days off to move house or volunteer for your favourite charity.

This role involves collecting and disseminating regulatory information, providing insights to internal stakeholders, and supporting the development of regulatory strategies. Supports the Senior Director, Regulatory Affairs (Labeling/Ad-Promo), in efforts to influence the regulatory environment.

Key Accountabilities

Proactively monitors and assesses global regulatory environments for emerging changes in laws, regulations, and guidance impacting drug and device development.
Tracks and evaluates updates from key regulatory authorities (e.g., FDA, EMA), industry associations, and external intelligence sources.
Maintains and continuously enhances regulatory intelligence databases and tools to ensure accurate, timely, and efficient dissemination of information.
Analyzes regulatory developments, including guidance documents, policies, and regulations, to determine potential impact on internal processes, development programs, and regulatory strategies. Anticipates and tracks regulatory changes over time, delivering timely, accurate, and actionable updates to impacted stakeholders across the organization.
Partners with Quality to ensure appropriate change control processes are initiated and tracked through implementation when regulatory changes impact internal procedures.
Translates complex regulatory information into clear, actionable insights for cross-functional stakeholders.
Develops and delivers regulatory intelligence communications, including newsletters, alerts, trackers, and periodic reports.
Responds to internal inquiries by providing tailored regulatory intelligence summaries and detailed analyses to support decision-making.
Leads and facilitates regulatory intelligence meetings to include review and discussion of ad hoc query requests, regulatory background package requests, health authority guidance, Federal Register notices, public commenting opportunities, newsletter content, training sessions, and knowledge-sharing forums.
Coordinates cross-functional discussions to evaluate the impact of new or revised regulatory requirements. Collaborates closely with key functions, including Quality, Pharmacovigilance, Clinical, CMC, and Regulatory Affairs, to ensure alignment and effective implementation.
Leads the regulatory public commenting process and identifies opportunities to engage with external stakeholders on draft regulations, guidance, and policies.
Supports the development, coordination, and submission of company comments to regulatory authorities and industry organizations.
Confirms the list of upcoming regulatory meetings/workshops/conferences remains current.
Drives continuous improvement of regulatory intelligence processes, systems, and tools to enhance efficiency and value. Authors and conducts periodic review of regulatory intelligence Standard Operating Procedures or work practices.
Manages and maintains internal knowledge management platforms (e.g., SharePoint, intranet) to ensure accessible and up-to-date information. Develops, reviews and updates the Regulatory Intelligence homepage on the Global Regulatory Affairs Portal.
Contributes to cross-functional initiatives and organizational projects by providing regulatory intelligence expertise and strategic insight.
Manages onboarding and offboarding of regulatory intelligence team members and provides input on team member performance. Provides leadership, coaching, and day‑to‑day oversight for direct reports within Global Regulatory Intelligence, fostering their professional growth and development.

Position Requirements

Education and Experience:

Bachelor's degree in life sciences, law, public policy, or a related field.
A Master's degree or higher is preferred.
Minimum 8 years’ experience in pharmaceutical regulatory affairs, including 6 years’ experience in regulatory intelligence.
Demonstrates solid working knowledge of the drug, biologic, and device development process, laws, regulations, and guidelines from FDA, EMA, PMDA, ICH, etc.
Demonstrates understanding of the major regional and global industry association priorities (e.g., PhRMA, EFPIA, JPMA, etc.).
Previous interactions with FDA or other health authority are desirable.
Proficient in using regulatory intelligence tools and databases.

Key Competencies

Analytical thinking, problem solving and decision making: Demonstrates strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to evaluate complex issues, identify risks and opportunities, develop practical and achievable solutions, and make sound, data-driven decisions
Strategic thinking & regulatory innovation: Capable of strategic thinking and proposing innovative solutions involving regulatory issues, while being a team player who invites response and discussion
Performance & accountability: Comfortable in a fast-paced, results-driven, and highly accountable work environment
Independence & team effectiveness: Demonstrated ability to work independently with minimal supervision while also contributing effectively as a collaborative team member. Balances individual accountability with a commitment to supporting team goals, sharing knowledge, and fostering a positive and productive work environment.
Attention to detail: Strong attention to detail, ensuring accuracy, quality, and consistency in all work products
Multitasking: Demonstrates the ability to effectively prioritize, organize, and manage multiple tasks, projects, and competing priorities simultaneously while meeting deadlines and maintaining high standards of performance

Key Capabilities

Commitment to excellence: Take pride in your work and consistently strive for excellence in everything you do
Results-oriented: Driven to achieve goals and objectives, with a strong focus on delivering measurable results
Creativity and innovation: Possess a willingness to think outside the box and come up with unique and creative solutions to challenges
Strong communication skills: Able to communicate effectively with colleagues and stakeholders at all levels, using clear and concise language
Collaboration: Work effectively as part of a team, actively sharing knowledge and expertise to achieve common goals
Resilience: Demonstrate the ability to bounce back from setbacks and persevere in the face of challenges
Inclusive mindset: Demonstrate an understanding and appreciation for diversity, and actively work to create an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and respected
Adaptability: Comfortable working in a dynamic environment, able to adjust to changing priorities, and willing to take on new challenges
Ethical behavior: Act with integrity and demonstrate a commitment to ethical behavior in all interactions with colleagues and stakeholders
Continuous learning: Show a commitment to ongoing learning and professional development, continually seeking out opportunities to expand your knowledge and skills

At Telix, we believe everyone counts
, we strive to be extraordinary
, and we pursue our goals with determination and integrity
. You will be part of an engaged and supportive group of colleagues who all have a shared purpose: to help people with cancer and rare diseases live longer, better quality lives.
Being a Telix employee means being a part of a unique, global, interdisciplinary team working to deliver what's next in precision medicine. We have hybrid and remote employees located all around the world. We offer competitive salaries, annual performance-based bonuses, an equity-based incentive program, generous vacation, paid wellness days and support for learning and development.

Telix Pharmaceuticals is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other legally protected characteristics.

new_jobs.title: Director Information Security
new_jobs.description:
The Director, Information Security (InfoSec) is responsible for leading and evolving the organisation's global information security function, ensuring the protection of corporate systems, employee productivity platforms, customer-facing products, data, and technology assets. This role will define and execute the security strategy, strengthen cyber resilience, manage security risk, and implement scalable security controls that support business growth and regulatory compliance.

The successful candidate will build and mature security capabilities from the ground up, improving legacy environments, embedding security best practices across the organisation, and ensuring robust monitoring, governance, and risk management frameworks are in place. Through strong leadership and technical expertise, this role will have a significant impact on safeguarding the organisation, supporting customer trust, and enabling secure business operations globally.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the global information security function and provide strategic direction across all security domains.
Develop and implement the organisation's information security strategy, operating model, and roadmap.
Oversee security for corporate platforms, including email, collaboration, and productivity tools.
Ensure the security of customer-facing products, applications, and technology services.
Build and mature security capabilities and processes, establishing scalable security programmes from the ground up.
Identify, assess, and mitigate cyber security risks through effective governance and risk management practices.
Lead vulnerability management, penetration testing, threat detection, and ongoing security monitoring activities.
Implement compensating controls to address audit findings, compliance requirements, and identified risks.
Improve and modernise legacy systems while maintaining appropriate security controls and business continuity.
Partner with technology, infrastructure, engineering, product, legal, privacy, and risk teams to embed security-by-design principles.
Lead incident response planning, preparedness, and crisis management activities.
Develop executive reporting, security metrics, and dashboards to communicate security posture and programme maturity.
Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing Information Security team.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

10+ years of experience in Information Security, Cyber Security, Technology Risk, or related technology leadership roles.
Experience building, transforming, or scaling security functions within growing organisations.
Strong technical foundation in infrastructure, IT operations, systems administration, networking, or network security.
Demonstrated experience leading security operations, vulnerability management, penetration testing, and incident response programmes.
Strong understanding of security frameworks and industry standards such as ISO 27001, NIST, CIS Controls, SOC 2, and PCI DSS.
Experience implementing governance, risk, and compliance frameworks, including audit remediation and compensating controls.
Knowledge of cloud security, identity and access management, application security, and secure software development practices.
Proven ability to communicate technical risks and security priorities to executive and non-technical stakeholders.
Strong leadership, stakeholder management, and team development capabilities.
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, CCSP, or equivalent are highly desirable.

Benefits

At Dye & Durham we strive to be visionaries! As a leader in our field, we ensure our employees are ready for the next challenge in their journey with us by offering internal and external training opportunities. We offer competitive salaries and a whole host of benefits including healthcare, pension, company discounts, wellness programs, and paid days off to move house or volunteer for your favourite charity.
